text:
Predicates:
InCity(x, y) ::: x is in city y.
InState(x, y) ::: x is in state y.
City(y) ::: y is a city.
State(y) ::: y is a state.
InSameState(x, y) ::: x and y are in the same state.
ExclusiveStates(x, y) ::: x and y are in different states, with no overlap.
UniqueState(x, y) ::: city x is only in city y.
Premises:
City(Billings) ∧ State(Montana) ∧ InCity(Billings, Montana) ::: Billings is a city in Montana.
State(Montana) ∧ City(Butte) ∧ City(Helena) ∧ City(Missoula) ::: Montana includes Butte, Helena, Missoula.
InCity(WhiteSulphurSprings, Montana) ∧ InCity(Butte, Montana) ::: White Sulphur Springs and Butte are in Montana.
City(StPierre) ∧ ¬InState(StPierre, Montana) ::: St Pierre is not in Montana.
∀x (InCity(x, Butte) → ¬InCity(x, StPierre)) ::: Any city in Butte is not in St Pierre.
∀x ∀y ((InCity(x, y) ∧ City(y)) → ∀z ((City(z) ∧ InCity(z, y)) → (z = x))) ::: Each city is only in one state, except for specified cities.
Conclusion:
InSameState(Butte, StPierre) ::: Butte and St Pierre are in the same state.
